paper.title: ChemAgent: Self-updating Library in Large Language Models Improves Chemical Reasoning
paper.central_claim: ChemAgent builds a planning/execution/knowledge library and dynamically enriches retained memories during reasoning, yielding better chemical reasoning and continued self-evolution across problems.
paper.scope_class: A: runtime feedback-gated planning/execution memory; B: development-set library construction

provenance.notes: Assigned model type sonnet maps to gpt-6.1-sol; environment identifies gpt-6.1-sol. No independent runtime receipt or session identifier exposed; actual_model left null per worker template. No model probing.

sections_read: Complete fixed HTML lines1–4665 through EOF: abstract, §§1–4, Algorithm1, Tables1–6, AppendicesA–H including full prompts and all three worked/decomposition examples. Figures5/6/8/9/10 plots are image-only; captions/prose read, no page_images in manifest and no unseen graph values invented.

evidence.quote: This component is generated temporarily during the solution of a specific task and is not intended for permanent retention.
evidence.support_explanation: Knowledge memory is temporary; retained-object claims concern planning and execution memory, not all three.

evidence.quote: In addition to ranking, we discard any memory units that do not meet a predefined confidence threshold, as evaluated by the LLMs.
evidence.support_explanation: Initial development library has a self-judged filter, not externally certified unit validity.

evidence.quote: Moreover, the memory is continuously updated with newly solved sub-tasks and their solutions during runtime.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit persistent case growth during use.

evidence.quote: The plan memory will be updated by a summary of the overall strategy knowledge used,
evidence.support_explanation: Planning abstraction complements concrete subtask cases.

evidence.quote: We evaluate the accuracy by comparing their outputs with the correct answers, using a relative tolerance of 0.01.
evidence.support_explanation: Ground-truth numeric endpoint is more direct than self-judge confidence.

evidence.quote: We allow ChemAgent to dynamically update and enrich its library during the test stage to analyze this self-evolution process.
evidence.support_explanation: Repeated test-stream adaptation, not a separately certified frozen online improver.

evidence.quote: all related responses and knowledge from that process are added to the library if the solution is correct.
evidence.support_explanation: Correctness admission uses outcome knowledge; availability and role must not be recast as autonomous label-free evaluation.

signatures.object: Persistent execution-case library and summarized planning memories; model parameters unchanged
signatures.information: Development problems+solutions, generated task decomposition, solved runtime subproblems, code outputs, numeric correctness, retrieved cases
signatures.operation: Split problems into conditions/query/subsolution units; LLM confidence filter and difficulty rank; retrieve Llama3-embedding neighbors; solve with Python; append successful units and summarize reusable strategy.
signatures.conditions: Useful transferable subtask structure; correctness labels or reliable self-evaluation; retrieval respects chemical constraints
signatures.feedback: Development solutions, Python outputs and model evaluation; runtime self-evolution admits whole-problem successes by correct-or-not outcome
signatures.selection_rule: Thresholded cosine retrieval; planning up to2 examples/execution up to4; confidence-ranked initial units; iteration experiment keeps correct solutions and excludes same-origin problem memory on future retries
signatures.selection_data: Dev9/10/16/8 problems; test39/49/107/34; runtime evolution reuses MATTER test items with outcome gates
signatures.persistence: Planning/execution memory retained and accumulated across tasks/iterations; knowledge memory temporary
signatures.later_use: Retrieved exemplars condition later subtask execution and decomposition, including other problems in subsequent iterations
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher numeric accuracy and gradual MATTER iteration improvement
signatures.failure_boundary: Cross-test label exposure, indirect leakage, similar-but-inapplicable precedents, erroneous synthetic units and no protected incumbent/rollback

signatures.object: Coverage of execution memory when no sufficiently similar case exists
signatures.information: Current subtask topic and base-model parametric chemistry knowledge
signatures.operation: Generate diverse related chemistry questions, worked solutions and executable Python examples; use as synthetic memory
signatures.conditions: Self-generated principles and solutions must be correct and useful
signatures.feedback: Model confidence and requested Python verification; external semantic validator not established
signatures.selection_rule: Fallback triggered by insufficient retrieved similarity; confidence/prompt constraints, no separately calibrated admission audit
signatures.selection_data: Test subtask topic and generated analogues
signatures.persistence: Library enrichment described; exact distinction between transient synthetic and globally admitted examples not fully operationalized
signatures.later_use: Assist subtask reasoning as execution-style memory
signatures.failure_boundary: Synthetic agreement can amplify wrong formulas; no isolated synthetic-fallback ablation

gap.author_gap: Fixed chemistry prompting and self-refinement fail to reuse analogous past solutions, causing repeated formula/unit/calculation errors.
gap.checked_gap: Reusable functional subtask cases plus planning summaries address a plausible recurrence bottleneck. Closest chemistry comparator StructChem is supplied only through this paper; generic external-memory novelty remains incremental and source-limited.

lineage.source_version: Fixed paper descriptions only; neighbor source versions unavailable

gap.residue: Subtask-granularity library with persistent planning/execution distinction, similarity fallback and runtime outcome-gated accumulation
gap.stakes: One incorrect formula, unit or precedent can cascade through a multi-step scientific answer.
gap.method_response: Split-and-retrieve precedents, summarize strategies, temporary knowledge checks and optional solution/plan refinement
gap.remaining_gap: Which part of improvement requires dynamic memory versus static exemplars and added evaluation compute remains unresolved; self-evolution revisits test tasks.

claims.text: ChemAgent improves chemical reasoning over baselines.
claims.setting: GPT4-1106-preview four SciBench chemistry sets,229 test problems total
claims.baseline/control: StructChem and direct/Python reasoning; reported baseline data partly inherited
claims.selection_vs_test: Initial library from43 dev problems; main test vs runtime-update usage not fully distinguished for every table
claims.result/denominator: Table1 macro57.16 vs47.66 StructChem (+9.50pp),19.48 direct (+37.68pp); CHEMMC74.36 vs28.21 (+46.15pp) on39 items. Not46% relative improvement or a pure runtime-memory effect.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported end-task gains for full system; static retrieval, decomposition and evaluation all contribute.

claims.text: Retained memory itself benefits later chemical tasks.
claims.setting: Dev-built library; GPT4 per-memory ablations and MATTER source swaps
claims.baseline/control: Table1 no eval52.12 vs no memory/no eval49.22 macro; Table2 full memory53.71 weighted vs none51.53; human few-shot replacement53.71; Table3 GPT4 memory44.89 vs GPT3.5 memory36.73 (GPT4 consumer)
claims.selection_vs_test: Dev-built units transferred to test; memory-source experiments not trained improver evaluation
claims.result/denominator: +2.90pp macro library gain; weighted memory improvement2.18pp but human replacement ties; hybrid GPT4 result28.57 on49 MATTER tests
claims.allowed_conclusion: Retained library and quality matter in some settings, but superiority over well-chosen static examples is not established.

claims.text: Self-updating library improves with repeated use.
claims.setting: MATTER49 test questions revisited over iterations, without evaluation/refinement
claims.baseline/control: Initial memory baseline44.89; each iteration twice
claims.selection_vs_test: Correct outcomes gate additions; own-problem-derived memories excluded on subsequent retries, but other test-derived memory remains
claims.result/denominator: Author reports upward convergence above44.89; exact Figure5 points unavailable in fixed text and not fabricated
claims.allowed_conclusion: Evidence of retained cross-item reuse in an oracle-gated repeated-test protocol, not independently heldout improver improvement.

claims.text: Benefits generalize across backbones and memory/evaluator designs.
claims.setting: GPT3.5 and open models; full AppendixB
claims.baseline/control: Direct versus ChemAgent and GPT3.5 refinement variants
claims.selection_vs_test: Open models use execution memory only, no evaluation/refinement; model names inconsistently7b/Llama3/Llama3.1 in prose/table
claims.result/denominator: Open macro17.41→25.75;29.48→42.52;43.47→53.58; ATKINS decreases22.43→19.63 for small Llama and57.01→56.07 for Qwen. GPT3.5 memory31.82→26.50 with self evaluator,31.01 GPT4 evaluator.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Average gains across models with clear negative domains/evaluator cases; not uniform or universal gains.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A development-built library of solved atomic cases and strategies is reused in later problems; controlled variants report modest memory-specific gains and sensitivity to memory source. Runtime accumulation is shown only with repeated MATTER tests and correctness gating.
unresolved: No clean independent post-update evaluation or stream-order replication; not improver-level certification.
Some metrics are macro averages while Table2 explicitly uses test-size weights; do not mix them.
AppendixH retains/certifies a concrete unit error; confidence and code executability do not ensure chemistry validity.
Numeric curves lack supplied page images; exact curves not needed for scoped conclusion.

G.reason: Concrete recurring formula/unit/precedent problem and closest chemistry baseline; novelty over generic memory methods incompletely established by supplied neighboring sources.

M.reason: Reconstructable case/strategy unit, retrieval, fallback and refinement prompts; feedback response fits recurrence but confidence calibration and persistent synthetic-unit admission remain weak.

X.reason: Retained later use, ablations and failure boundaries described; retention/provenance, thresholds and recovery controls incomplete. Matching cards earns no points.

E.measurement.reason: Numeric tolerance against ground truth directly measures chemical answers; published library/example unit error and uncalibrated confidence temper semantic-verifier trust, without negating endpoint accuracy.

E.causality.reason: Memory-off/type/source and evaluator variants informative; strong human-example tie and unmatched extra calls prevent unique dynamic-memory attribution.

E.holdout.reason: Explicit43-dev/229-test split supports initial retention; runtime experiment repeats49 tests with correctness-based admission, only own-origin guard. No independent new-item post-update evaluation.

E.statistics.reason: Open experiments repeated≥3 times; evolution twice with difference bars and shot variance discussed; no main-result CIs or independent search/order variance. Auxiliary similarity p-values are association tests, not significance of main gains.
search_scope: Complete main results, Figure5/9 captions, AppendicesB/C/D/F: limited repeats, auxiliary tests, no main CIs/order variance

E.cost.reason: 12k/$0.09 versus23k/$0.1725 per question reported; initial library and repeated evolution cost omitted, no full budget-matched alternative.

reason: Complete fixed text supports in-scope persistent library review. Missing image-only exact curve values do not prevent scoped review; no independent reproduction claimed.
